abstract: Huntingtons disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in HTT, but how PolyQ expansion alters huntingtin behaviour in human neurons remains unclear. We combined live single-molecule imaging and tracking with transformer-based motion profiling to resolve full-length HTT dynamics in pluripotent hESCs and their derived cortical- and MSN-like neurons. HTT occupied three behavioural states: bound, confined, and exploratory. PolyQ expansion progressively shifted molecules from bound and confined states toward the exploratory state. These effects emerged at shorter PolyQ lengths in MSN-like neurons, and only at 150Q included faster exploratory diffusion and impaired return to stable bound or confined states. Tag-swap experiments showed that mt- HTT imposed similar defects on co-expressed wild-type HTT (wt-HTT), revealing a dominant effect of the HD mutation on wt-HTT dynamics. Loss of HTT (HTT-/-) or expression of mt-HTT also altered kinesin and myosin dynamics, consistent with changes in the intracellular environment of HD cells. Thus, PolyQ-expanded HTT does not merely acquire abnormal dynamics, it leads to a broader disruption of the cytoplasmic environment in which both wt-HTT and molecular motors operate.
